title: How to enlarge cursor in Linear on Mac: simple system settings for better visibility
metaTitle: How to enlarge cursor in Linear on Mac
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor in Linear on Mac by adjusting your system-wide accessibility settings. Follow our simple guide to improve your screen visibility.
intro: You cannot enlarge the cursor directly inside the Linear app because it uses your macOS system pointer. To change the size, you must adjust your Mac system-wide accessibility settings.
tldr: Linear does not have an internal cursor size setting.
Open System Settings on your Mac.
Navigate to Accessibility and then Display.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preference.
This change applies to Linear and all other apps.

blocks.text: Why Linear does not have a cursor setting

The Linear desktop application for macOS is built as an Electron wrapper. This means it functions like a web browser displaying the Linear web application. Because it is a web-based interface, it inherits the default cursor behavior from your operating system. There is no setting within Linear to override this behavior, as the app is designed to feel like a native part of your desktop environment.

Many users search for an internal setting because they notice the cursor changing shape when hovering over different elements. Linear allows you to toggle between a native arrow and a web-style hand icon. This is located in your account preferences under General, then Interface and theme. Changing this only affects the icon shape, not the physical size of the pointer on your screen.

Since Linear relies on macOS for its pointer, you must change your system settings to make the cursor larger. This is a universal change. Once you apply the setting, the cursor will be larger in every application, including your browser, code editor, and the Linear desktop app.

It is common to confuse the Linear project management tool with other apps that have similar names. Some users search for cursor settings thinking they are using LinearMouse, a utility for customizing mouse behavior. Others might be looking for Cursor, which is an AI-powered code editor. Neither of these tools is related to the Linear project management software. If you are trying to change how your mouse works, check if you have those third-party apps installed.

If you do not want a permanently large cursor, you can use the shake to locate feature. This is also found in the Accessibility settings. When you move your mouse quickly or shake your finger on the trackpad, the cursor will temporarily grow in size. This makes it much easier to find your place on a busy screen without needing a massive pointer all the time.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor size only for Linear?
faq.answer: No. Because Linear uses the system cursor, any change you make to the pointer size will apply to every app on your Mac.

faq.question: Does the Linear desktop app have different settings than the web version?
faq.answer: No. Both the desktop app and the web version use the same system-level cursor settings.

faq.question: Will changing my cursor size affect my click accuracy?
faq.answer: Usually, no. macOS handles the click point at the tip of the arrow, even if the arrow itself is larger.

task: How to enlarge the cursor size for the Linear application on macOS.
appliesTo: Linear desktop app for macOS (all versions).

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen and select System Settings.

steps.name: Access Accessibility
steps.text: In the sidebar, scroll down and click on Accessibility.

steps.name: Open Display settings
steps.text: Click the Display option within the Accessibility menu.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer size
steps.text: Locate the Pointer section and move the Pointer size slider to the right to increase your cursor size.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor is still small in Linear.
troubleshooting.fix: Restart the Linear app after changing your system settings to ensure the change takes effect.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find the Pointer settings.
troubleshooting.fix: Ensure you are looking in Accessibility > Display, not just the general Display settings.

lazur.spoken: Where do I change the pointer size?
lazur.result: Lazur will circle the Pointer size slider in your Accessibility settings.
